parameterEdits.find: a title, a degree, a certificate or a span of years the CV does not show.
parameterEdits.replace: a span of years, a title, a degree or a certificate that the CV or the certificate text CONTRADICTS - meaning the record addresses the same fact and shows less (typed 5 years against 3 dated years; a Master's claimed where the CV lists a Bachelor's). A factual claim in the cover letter that the record contradicts counts the same way. SILENCE IS NOT CONTRADICTION: a skill, language, certificate or any other qualification the candidate typed or wrote in the cover letter that the record simply does not mention is UNVERIFIED - it earns no credit and is NEVER an integrity_concern. NOT MEETING AN EMPLOYER EXPECTATION IS NOT CONTRADICTION either: living in another city than the job, having fewer years than required, or holding a different title than the vacancy is a criterion result, never an integrity_concern - integrity is only about the candidate's OWN claims against the record. The "Job applied for" line is the employer's vacancy, not a claim about the candidate's own title: never quote it in an integrity_concern and never compare it with the CV to raise one.

parameterEdits.find: - For anything the record can show -- the role itself, experience, skills, education, career level, management track, industry, employer, certifications, location -- a claim the CV does NOT corroborate is at most `partial`, NEVER `met`. Typing "Senior Petroleum Engineer" in the position field while the CV shows no engineering role is `partial` at best. parameterEdits.replace:
- For anything the record can show -- the role itself, experience, skills, education, career level, management track, industry, employer, certifications, languages -- a claim made ONLY in an application field or the cover letter earns nothing: set "not_assessed", never "partial" or "met", and open the evidence with "Application field (self-reported): claimed ..., not shown in the CV or certificates" or "Cover letter: ...". When the record supports it at all, judge it on the record alone - the claim never raises the status. Where the record actively contradicts the claim, that is "missing", with an integrity_concern only as the SECURITY paragraph allows.
- LOCATION keeps its own rule: a typed location the CV does not corroborate is at most "partial", NEVER "met"; where the CV actively contradicts the location the candidate typed, that is "missing" AND an integrity_concern; a CV location that simply differs from the employer's expected location is "missing" only, never an integrity_concern.
